metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: Data ('available from the corresponding author upon request')
metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores) ('server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650')

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic volumes and driving behavior data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters in SUMO.
nodes_source.size_estimate: Traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in 10-minute intervals.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper explicitly states in the Data Availability section that data are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Video frame extraction to position matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Raw video frames are converted into position matrices (mt) where vehicle coordinates are set to a constant value and non-vehicle positions are zeroed.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, coordinate extraction technique is unnamed but data representation is clear.

nodes_process.source_quote: After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4   512 in pixels. *ree consecutive observations are stacked
nodes_process.description: Stacking three consecutive binary matrices into a single tensor and downsampling for input dimension reduction while retaining positional information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, input dimensions and frame count specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer
nodes_process.description: Neural network architecture comprising three CNN layers with ReLu followed by twin FC heads for Q-values and speed/queue length predictions.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, Figure 7 and text detail layers, filters, strides, and units.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Agent training using DRL with experience replay and a target network. Minimizes total loss consisting of Bellman error and auxiliary multitask regression.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, nearly all hyperparameters specified in Table 1; versioning is only missing item.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Simulation experiment on a modeled Qingdao tunnel freeway merge. Comparison of DRL, no-control, and PI-ALINEA baseline over 20 experiments.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, simulator named, parameters documented, but scenario road network files not available.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8 presents the training process of the Q-network... The episode reward and mean travel time are both converged in 400,000 training frames.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence plots showing (a) episode reward and (b) mean mainline travel time (seconds) versus the number of training frames (up to 1M).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Model training procedures and SUMO simulation parameters are specified, but specific source traffic demand data for calibration is not provided in a raw format.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline travel time distribution (interquartile range) time-series from 8:00 to 9:00 for three scenarios: No control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Results follow from the defined DRL reward function and SUMO environment; traffic counts for the simulation scenario available upon request only.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times (s) for each of the 20 simulation trials under No controls, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL, including percent reduction metrics.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Explicit trial results provided, but exact source traffic counts for initialization and calibration are omitted.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal-spatial speed heatmaps comparing three scenarios: (a) no-control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL across freeway distance (0-4000m) and time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plausible outcome based on described lane-metering DRL architecture, but specific spatial sensor layouts/indices are implied by subareas later.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series (8:00-9:00) of vehicle queue length distribution on the on-ramp for three scenarios, showing impact of ramp metering.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Coherent aggregate of simulation metrics based on specified rewards (μ and ω in Eq. 7).

nodes_sink.source_quote: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot showing relationship between the proportion of the red phase (red ratio %) and the mean queue length (m) for two methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulated trial data with explicit control phase measurements.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area
nodes_sink.description: Correlation between occupancy (%) and queue length (m) over time for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL, featuring Pearson correlation coefficients (rho).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Direct statistical measurement from simulation results; clear correlation logic presented.

nodes_sink.description: Box plot distribution of traffic volume (veh/h) downstream of the merge area at discrete time steps for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Reproducibility constrained by specific traffic count calibration values used in SUMO environment setup.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Box plot of mainline travel time under 8 spatial information perturbation scenarios compared to a baseline, demonstrating agent reliance on regional visual data.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure for perturbing the spatial sub-matrices (zeroing input subareas) is explicitly defined and well-supported.
